assertions.assert: By default it decodes through the OpenAI-compatible API: the speech service's `decode` with provider `null` and model `nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b` (the lab's Nemotron), `POST {base}/audio/transcriptions`. The service's `bot.ability.hearing.speech.decoding.output` `{text}` is answered to its parent as `bot.ability.hearing.speech.decoding.output` exactly `{id, text}` (the request's `id`, the answer's `text`, trimmed). It is long-lived: each utterance is a request `bot.ability.hearing.speech.decoding.input` `{id, audio, media_type?}`.
Speech the backend heard none of decodes to empty words: `{id, text: ""}`, not a failure.

The `provider` and `model` `<param>`s choose the backend: provider `gemini` is Gemini's `POST {base}/interactions`, whose answer's `output_text`, or its `model_output` steps' text, trimmed, becomes the answer's `text`; provider `null` is the OpenAI-compatible `POST {base}/audio/transcriptions` and never calls Gemini's.

When the service answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message}` (an unreadable or empty audio file, an error status, a malformed answer), it answers `bot.ability.failed` exactly `{id, message}` with the service's message.
When the decoder cannot run (a malformed `media_type` rejects its start with `error.execution`), it answers `bot.ability.failed` `{id, message: "SpeechDecoding could not run (<error event>)"}`.
